Just thought I'd let people know this, in case you don't already. When you use either of the sites that show deleted comments - either unreddit or r.go1dfish.me, a connection is made from your machine to reddit. That connection includes reddit's domain cookies (edit: note comment from go1dfish below, cookies from reddit.com are not sent to oauth.reddit.com), which means they log it as a view for your user account if you're still logged in. And if you're not logged in, they still get your IP.

I just want to point this out because it's different from what archive.is does - that site actually stores a copy of the pages it archives, so when you view the archive, the owner of the original site doesn't know about you.

This distinction may or may not be of interest to you, but now you know it exists.
FYI: both unreddit and r.go1dfish.me connect from your machine to reddit.

This is true, my app works by using the reddit API and comparing that against historical data at pushshift.io's API (that it grabbed via reddit's API as well).

I tend to call it an app rather than a site because technically it works much more like Alien Blue or Reddit is Fun than it does like Voat or Reddit itself.

It's a reddit client built in javascript that uses another api service (pushshift.io) and the reddit api (to access data from /r/undelete+longtail) to restore moderator removed content. It's an application registered with reddit that follows all of reddit's terms of use and API rules. It clearly identifies itself to reddit as well and they could choose to shut it (or pushshift.io) down at any time.

That connection includes reddit's domain cookies, which means they log it as a view for your user account if you're still logged in.

This is not true for my app, it uses the OAUTH reddit API and this does not send your regular cookies along side. The requests made by my app are all unauthenticated but it is true they are coming from your IP address and could be linked up that way.
